# Ubuntu Desktop

> This is the documentation for Ubuntu Desktop, an open-source operating system powering millions of PCs and laptops around the world.


2026

- [Adjust the contrast](how-to/accessibility/adjust-the-contrast/index.html.md): Turn on high contrast in Ubuntu Desktop to make windows and buttons easier to see without changing the screen brightness.

- [Turn on bounce keys](how-to/accessibility/turn-on-bounce-keys/index.html.md): Turn on bounce keys to ignore rapidly repeated key presses, for example if hand tremors cause you to press a key twice.
- [Magnify a screen area](how-to/accessibility/magnify-a-screen-area/index.html.md): Turn on the zoom feature to magnify part of the screen in Ubuntu Desktop, and adjust magnification, mouse tracking, crosshairs and colors.

- [Use an on-screen keyboard](how-to/accessibility/use-an-on-screen-keyboard/index.html.md): Turn on the on-screen keyboard in Ubuntu Desktop to type without a physical keyboard, and enter symbols or change input sources.
- [Adjust the double-click speed](how-to/accessibility/adjust-the-double-click-speed/index.html.md): Change how quickly you must press the mouse button twice to double-click on Ubuntu Desktop, and check for a faulty mouse.
- [Simulate clicking by hovering](how-to/accessibility/simulate-clicking-by-hovering/index.html.md): Turn on Hover Click to click or drag by holding the pointer over a control, and adjust the delay and motion threshold.
- [Change text size on the screen](how-to/accessibility/change-text-size-on-the-screen/index.html.md): Make text larger in Ubuntu Desktop using Large Text, Tweaks or application shortcuts if you have difficulty reading the screen.
- [Simulate a right mouse click](how-to/accessibility/simulate-a-right-mouse-click/index.html.md): Turn on simulated secondary click to right-click by holding down the left mouse button, and set how long you must hold it.
- [Click and move the mouse pointer using the keypad](how-to/accessibility/click-and-move-the-mouse-pointer-using-the-keypad/index.html.md): Turn on Mouse Keys to move the pointer and click using the numeric keypad if you can't use a mouse or other pointing device.
- [Manage repeated key presses](how-to/accessibility/manage-repeated-key-presses/index.html.md): Control how a key repeats when you hold it down on Ubuntu Desktop by turning repeat keys off or changing the delay and speed.
- [Navigate the interface using the keyboard](how-to/accessibility/navigate-the-interface-using-the-keyboard/index.html.md): Use only the keyboard to launch and switch applications, navigate menus and move around the Ubuntu Desktop interface without a mouse.
- [Read the screen in Braille](how-to/accessibility/orca/read-screen-in-braille/index.html.md): Set up Orca with a Braille display through BRLTTY, use display commands, change the language table and fix detection problems.
- [Add, edit, or remove dictionary entries](how-to/accessibility/orca/add-dictionary-entries/index.html.md): Add, edit or remove entries in the Orca pronunciation dictionary to fix words that your speech synthesizer mispronounces.
- [Read documents and web pages using the screen reader](how-to/accessibility/orca/read-documents-and-web-pages-using-the-screen-reader/index.html.md): Use Orca commands to browse web pages, read in caret mode, check formatting, fill forms, read tables and follow live regions.
- [Read the screen aloud](how-to/accessibility/orca/read-screen-aloud/index.html.md): Turn on the Orca screen reader in Ubuntu Desktop so it speaks the user interface, and find out how to install and control it.

- [Spellcheck preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-spellcheck/index.html.md): Configure how Orca presents spell checker information, such as spelling misspelled words and suggestions and speaking error context.
- [Speech preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-speech/index.html.md): Configure Orca speech preferences, including enabling speech, verbosity, punctuation level and spoken context.
- [Screen reader preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/index.html.md): Reference for Orca preferences that customize screen reader behavior in all applications, such as key echo, speech, Braille and voices.
- [Profiles](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-profile/index.html.md): Manage multiple Orca configurations with profiles, and choose how progress bar updates are spoken, shown in Braille or beeped.
- [Voice preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-voice/index.html.md): Configure Orca voice preferences, including voice types, the speech system and synthesizer, plus person, rate, pitch and volume.
- [Chat preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-chat/index.html.md): Configure how Orca behaves in instant messaging and IRC chat clients, such as announcing chatroom names and typing status.
- [Text attributes preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-text-attributes/index.html.md): Configure which text attributes Orca speaks or shows in Braille, such as font, style and alignment, and reorder or reset them.
- [Key bindings preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-key-binding/index.html.md): Configure Orca key bindings, including the Orca Modifier keys, the key bindings table and unbound commands.
- [General preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-general/index.html.md): Configure Orca general preferences, including the keyboard layout that sets the Orca Modifier and how tooltips are presented.
- [Key echo preferences](reference/accessibility/orca-preferences/orca-preferences-key-echo/index.html.md): Configure Orca key echo to choose whether keys, characters, words or sentences are spoken as you type.
